question_en: A company has an unsecured line of credit and needs to maintain its EBIT-to-interest coverage ratio greater than 2.0. Its EBIT is estimated to be between $36 million and $48 million, with all values equally likely. If the forecasted interest charge for the year is $20 million, the probability that EBIT/interest will be more than 2.0 is closest to:
explanation_en:
The EBIT-to-interest ratio is equal to 2.0 when the EBIT is $40 million. Given that the values
between $36 million and $48 million are equally likely, the probability of the ratio being equal to
or less than2.0 is 33.3% (= [$40 million–$36 million]/[$48 million–$36 million]). Consequently,
the probability of the ratio being greater than 2.0 is 66.7% (i.e., 1 – Probability of the ratio being
equal to or less than 2.0).

explanation_en:

question_en: Use the following values from a student's t-distribution to establish a 95% confidence interval for the population mean given a sample size of 10, a sample mean of 6.25, and a sample standard deviation of 12. Assume that the population from which the sample is drawn is normally distributed and the population variance is not known. The 95% confidence interval is closest to a
option_a: lower bound of–2.20 and an upper bound of 14.70.
option_b: lower bound of–2.33 and an upper bound of 14.83.
option_c: lowerbound of–0.71 and an upper bound of 13.21.
explanation_en: With a sample size of 10, there are 9 degrees of freedom. The confidence interval concept is based on a two-tailed approach. For a 95% confidence interval, 2.5% of the distribution will be in each tail. Thus, the correct t-statistic to use is 2.262. The confidence interval is calculated as: Xt S/ n 0.025 where X is the sample mean, s is the sample standard deviation, and n is the sample size. In this case: 6.25 ± 2.262 × 12/√10 = 6.25± 8.58369 or–2.33 to 14.83.
